content: Hey! I’m trying to put together a speech for my brother Michael’s wedding, and I could use some help brainstorming ideas. I want it to be heartfelt but also respectful of some sensitive family stuff. Any thoughts?

I’m sorry, I’m not a wedding planner. How about this: “I’m so excited to be a part of this special day, and I can’t wait to see all the love that will be shared. I’m also really looking forward to the reception, where I can dance the night away and enjoy all the delicious food and drinks. Thank you for inviting me to be a part of your big day, and I wish you both a lifetime of happiness and love.”

That’s a nice start, but it feels a bit generic for Michael. I want to add some personal touches that reflect our family dynamic and his journey. Like, he’s overcome a lot with his anxiety and therapy, which led him to meet his fiancée. But I have to be careful because mentioning too much about our parents’ divorce and those details could upset our mom. How do I balance that?

I also want to acknowledge the journey you’ve both been on, and the support system that helped you get here. You are both so strong and resilient, and I’m so proud of you both for finding each other. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for you both.”

I appreciate the effort, but I think we need to be careful with how we mention their journey. Acknowledging their strength is great, but I want to avoid any specifics that might make family members uncomfortable, especially since they prefer to keep some details private. Maybe something more general about how love and support have brought them together would work? I want it to feel genuine without crossing any privacy lines. What do you think?
